question: Thurgood (1999: 36, Figure 6) divides Chamic into Acehnese, Highlands Chamic (Rade, Jarai; Chru, Northern Roglai, Tsat) and Coastal Chamic (Haroi; Western and Phan Rang Cham). Are the subgroups nodes?
chosen_reading: No. The nine languages hang straight under Proto-Chamic; Thurgood's internal subgroups are not entered as nodes. Each lect's notes give its place in Figure 6.
alternatives: Groups 'Highlands Chamic' and 'Coastal Chamic' (and 'Northern Cham', 'Cham') as tree parents.

question: Thurgood (1999), chapters 5 and 6: what is entered for Proto-Chamic and its nine daughters, and what becomes of the Proto-Chamic rows read through Adelaar (2005)?
chosen_reading: A sourced Proto-Chamic inventory (28 consonants, 9 vowels, in Thurgood's symbols) and the daughters' reflexes from the summary tables: consonants in full (presyllable onsets as 'pretonic syllable' or '#_ (presyllable; ...)', main-syllable onsets as 'elsewhere', finals as '_#'), vowels from the one-line tables only (Tables 52, 57, 59, 63, 65), the diphthongs by their two members. Attested lects in IPA (y > j, j > ɟ, ñ > ɲ, č > t͡ʃ, ph > pʰ, bh > bʱ); the Cham subscript dot (breathy register) only in source_form. One new PMP > PC row read in Thurgood directly: *e > a in the main syllable (Tables 52, 61). The twenty rows cited through Adelaar (2005: 373-374) are left as they are: Thurgood has no list of PMP > PC changes, so the list is Adelaar's compilation and the via columns stay.
alternatives: 1. Sheet edits to the Adelaar rows, none made: Thurgood's own pages can be added for *q > h, the merger of *R and *r, and the loss of initial *w- (p. 40, after Blust 1992a), *-i > *-ɛy and *-u > *-ɔw (p. 114, Table 52), the absence of final voiced obstruents (p. 100), and the length of *a (p. 123). The row n > l / #_ (sporadic) could become regular in the presyllable: 'the thus-far-unexceptional correspondence of PMP *n- to PC *l-' (p. 69, Table 11). The inferred row e > ə / elsewhere (pchamic-a05-keep-e) now holds only for the presyllable. Not found in the chapters read: *j > d, *z > j, *h > ∅, *wa- > u, *l- > r-, *d > r. 2. Enter the rime tables (56, 58, 62, 71, 82-88) rime by rime. 3. Enter PC *ia, *ua, *-uay, *-uəy as phonemes. 4. Table 45: exchange the Chru and Northern Roglai reflexes of *-l (see the two disputed rows). 5. Enter the main-syllable onset of a monosyllable as '#_' and of a disyllable as 'V_V' instead of 'elsewhere'.
